newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open firmer on U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open firmer on U.S. data.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened slightly firmer in light trading on Wednesday after the release of economic data showing moderate inflationary pressures in the U.S. economy, traders said.
The U.S. Labor Department reported that the monthly Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.1 percent in June compared with a 0.1 percent increase in May.
Analysts said the slight increase in June was greeted favorably by the markets.
"The inflation numbers were perhaps a little bit lower than expected," said a trader at a large Canadian bank.
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill traded flat to yield 3.25 percent from 3.25 percent at Tuesday's close. The three-month cash T-bill fell to yield 3.21 percent.
Activity was light in the Canadian money market this morning with many accounts absent and trading largely dealer driven.
"There isn't anything huge going on," the trader said.
Analysts said the likelihood of another Bank of Canada interest rate hike was continuing to weigh on prices.
The central bank raised interest rates 25 basis points three weeks ago in an effort to cushion the Canadian dollar.
"As the market moves a little bit stronger, there is still the overhanging concern that the Bank of Canada is lurking in the background," the trader said.
"Nobody is going to try riding this for too long, so you can expect to see a little bit of profit-taking going on," the trader added.
Economic reports which will be closely watched by the market include Canada's consumer price index for June out on Thursday, and Friday's merchandise and wholesale trade data.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill dropped to yield 3.56 percent from a 3.57 percent yield at Tuesday's close. The one-year T-bill jumped to yield 4.07 percent from 4.10 percent.
The call loan or overnight lending rate traded at 3.30 percent, in the upper range of the Bank of Canada's 3.0-3.5 percent target range.
